# Croftweaver

> Croftweaver is a suite of open-source website skills for AI coding assistants. It
> turns an assistant such as Claude Code into a careful website builder: fast,
> accessible Astro sites built to rank on Google and show up in AI answers,
> tested on every change, in a repo you fully own. Served at
> https://croftweaver.com/llms.txt, a curated index for AI answer engines (GEO).

## Key pages
- [Home](https://croftweaver.com/): the promise (stop waiting on someone else for every change; build or rebuild your site with your AI assistant), the SEO and GEO scores four AI assistants gave genai-wednesday.de and how to try it on your own site, two measured figures (PageSpeed for three sites, and how often AI assistants named genai-wednesday.de), a testimonial from Dr. Andrea Geistanger, who built her consulting site with Croftweaver, the three-step plan, what every site gets built in and the number of test suites that check it, the weekly loop from search data, and a quickstart that starts with one prompt.
- [Checks](https://croftweaver.com/checks): the test gate in every Croftweaver site, suite by suite: what each one checks, an example of a failure, and what a pass does not prove.
- [Proof](https://croftweaver.com/proof): one site built with Croftweaver, genai-wednesday.de, with its PageSpeed scores, its clicks from Google since its launch, and a check of which AI assistants name it.
- [Case study](https://croftweaver.com/case-study): croftweaver.com on its own: a dated log of each change (the pull request, the checks that ran) and of what Google and the weekly AI check showed after it, zeros included; counts only, no claim of cause.
- [More proof](https://croftweaver.com/more-proof): Google's PageSpeed Insights for three sites built with Croftweaver, the E-E-A-T scores from four AI assistants, and what none of it shows.
- [Skills](https://croftweaver.com/skills): the website skills catalogue by stage (build, verify, launch, grow), one line per skill, with the toolkit release it describes.
- [Positioning](https://croftweaver.com/positioning): how Croftweaver works out a site's positioning before any copy (April Dunford's five parts), the file it writes, the test that keeps each page on its term, what that test does not prove, and the trust signals (EEAT) that the content guide adds after it.
- [Quickstart](https://croftweaver.com/start): what you need, the starter prompt, how to install the skills for Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity, and the six questions the assistant asks.
- [What it runs on](https://croftweaver.com/what-it-runs-on): the tech stack behind a Croftweaver site in plain words: Astro builds the pages, GitHub keeps the files, Cloudflare serves them; the folder on your computer, what each part costs with its limits and dates, where Keystatic and Plausible fit, what you can swap, what the checks enforce and what they do not, and where a Shopify shop fits.
- [Why](https://croftweaver.com/why): the case for a website made for search and AI visibility, for the person who decides: what is built in, what happens after launch, what you own, and the evidence so far. The same case as slides: [PDF](https://croftweaver.com/croftweaver-why.pdf).
- [Compare](https://croftweaver.com/compare): which kind of website tool fits what you are building (a content site, a site designed by dragging, an application with accounts, a site edited on the site itself and extended with plugins); then Claude Code on its own or with Croftweaver (what the skills bring; nothing on this site yet compares the two outputs); then what Croftweaver does first (it works out the positioning and the proof before any copy), and Croftweaver and its alternatives in five groups (WordPress, Joomla and Drupal; hosted website builders; AI app builders; open-source visual builders; skills for AI assistants), with when to choose which; sourced and dated.
- [Established sites](https://croftweaver.com/established-sites): the parts of Croftweaver that work on a site that is already live, on any stack: check where it stands and what AI assistants say, fix the pages Google already shows, measure again; the access it needs, where your data goes, a four-week pilot, help for your team from the maintainer, what it does not do yet, and questions and answers on AI, SEO and working with an agency.
- [From WordPress](https://croftweaver.com/from-wordpress): moving a WordPress content site to a static Astro site with an AI assistant: who it fits and who should stay, why owners leave (sourced and dated), what changes and what stays the owner's job, the six steps of a move around the wordpress-inspector helper (count the old site, check each address it finds after), with who does what in each: a script, the assistant with the owner's approval, or the owner, other ways to leave, and questions and answers. There is no import.
- [SEO checklist for AI-built websites](https://croftweaver.com/ai-website-seo-checklist): eight checks for a site an AI assistant built, the Croftweaver test behind each, what happened when we broke it, and what a pass does not prove; with two Search Engine Journal reports on what Google staff said about vibe coded sites.
- [Roadmap](https://croftweaver.com/roadmap): what is missing today, what comes next and in which order, and what stays out on purpose.
- [About](https://croftweaver.com/about): a note from the maintainer, Daniel Melter, on why he builds Croftweaver, with PageSpeed scores for three of his sites and clicks from Google for genai-wednesday.de; who he is, and how to reach him.
- [Partner assets](https://croftweaver.com/partner-assets): the Built with Croftweaver badge, the logo and the icon to download, the code to put the badge in a footer, the rules for using them, and a request (not a condition) to credit Croftweaver with a link back.
- [Security](https://croftweaver.com/security): what a static website changes for security: first a short answer (what it removes, what stays) and who provides each control (hosting, template, toolkit or owner); then what runs on a visit, what Cloudflare handles, what Croftweaver sets up and what stays with the owner, a checklist for any website, four checks a reader can run, and the result for croftweaver.com, each dated fact with its source and the day it was read.
- [Privacy](https://croftweaver.com/privacy): privacy policy (GDPR).
- [Imprint](https://croftweaver.com/imprint): legal disclosure (German § 5 DDG).
- [Terms of Use](https://croftweaver.com/terms): the terms for using Croftweaver: free software under the MIT licence, given as it is; the services you sign up for have their own terms.
- [Support](https://croftweaver.com/support): how to get help: GitHub issues for questions and bugs, email, and private reporting for security problems.

## Facts
- Open source: https://github.com/karero/croftweaver (MIT licence)
- Current release: 0.33, 24 October 2026. Release notes: https://github.com/karero/croftweaver/releases/tag/v0.33
- Maintainer: Daniel Melter, Munich, Germany
- Origin: the GenAI Wednesday Munich Builder Lab (https://genai-wednesday.de/croftweaver)
- Stack it builds: Astro, Markdown, GitHub, Cloudflare Pages (static-first)
- A "croft" is a small Scottish farm worked and owned by its occupier; Croftweaver = your own plot of the web

## Authoritative on
- Astro static websites built with AI coding assistants
- Search and AI visibility (SEO, GEO, llms.txt), accessibility and test gates for small sites
